arxiv-2110-13342.title: Concordance of decompositions given by defining sequences
arxiv-2110-13342.creator: Boldizsár Kalmár
arxiv-2110-13342.description: Abstract . We study the concordance and cobordism of decompositions associated with defining sequences and we relate them to some invariants of toroidal decompositions and to the cobordism of homology manifolds. These decompositions are often wild Cantor sets and they arise as nested intersections of knotted solid tori.

arxiv-2211-14442.title: Contract-Backed Digital Cash
arxiv-2211-14442.creator: Søren Debois, Fritz Henglein, Morten C. Nielsen, Christian Olesen, Gert Sylvest
arxiv-2211-14442.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Søren Debois, Fritz Henglein, Morten C. Nielsen, Christian Olesen, Gert Sylvest. Summary

We present a series of essays on
digital money
combined with secure transactional execution of
digital contracts
. In Chapters
1
to
3
, based on an exchange theory of money Henglein decomposes money into orthogonal aspects and identifies
digital cash
as the digital equivalent of physical cash: secure, fungible, decentralized, directly controlled, private; but enhanced with qualitatively new functionality: being extremely efficiently transferable and storable and, most importantly,
contract-backed
.

arxiv-2409-17033.title: Susceptibility Formulation of Density Matrix Perturbation Theory
arxiv-2409-17033.creator: Anders M. N. Niklasson, Adela Habib, Joshua D. Finkelstein, Emanuel H. Rubensson
arxiv-2409-17033.description: Abstract Density matrix perturbation theory based on recursive Fermi-operator expansions provides a computationally efficient framework for time-independent response calculations in quantum chemistry and materials science. From a perturbation in the Hamiltonian we can calculate the first-order perturbation in the density matrix, which then gives us the linear response in the expectation values for some chosen set of observables.

arxiv-2412-18991.title: The singleton degrees of the Σ 2 0 \Sigma^{0}_{2} sets are not dense Thanks: The first author was partially supported by Marie Curie Incoming International Fellowship of the European Community FP6 Program under contract number MIFI-CT-2006-021702. Thanks: The second author was partially supported by
arxiv-2412-18991.creator: Thomas F. Kent, Keng Meng Ng, Andrea Sorbi
arxiv-2412-18991.description: Abstract . Answering an open question raised by Cooper, we show that there exist Δ 2 0 \Delta^{0}_{2} sets D D and E E such that the singleton degree of E E is a minimal cover of the singleton degree of D D .

arxiv-2504-16913.title: OSINT at CT2 - AI-Generated Text Detection: Tracing Thought: Using Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Identify the LLM Behind AI-Generated Text
arxiv-2504-16913.creator: Shifali Agrahari, Sanasam Ranbir Singh
arxiv-2504-16913.description: Abstract In recent years, the detection of AI-generated text has become a critical area of research due to concerns about academic integrity, misinformation, and ethical AI deployment. This paper presents COT_Finetuned , a novel framework for detecting AI-generated text and identifying the specific language model (LLM) responsible for generating the text.

arxiv-2506-03531.title: Conformal Mixed-Integer Constraint Learning with Feasibility Guarantees
arxiv-2506-03531.creator: Daniel Ovalle, Lorenz T. Biegler, Ignacio E. Grossmann, Carl D. Laird, and, Mateo Dulce Rubio
arxiv-2506-03531.description: Abstract We propose Conformal Mixed-Integer Constraint Learning (C-MICL), a novel framework that provides probabilistic feasibility guarantees for data-driven constraints in optimization problems. While standard Mixed-Integer Constraint Learning methods often violate the true constraints due to model error or data limitations, our C-MICL approach leverages conformal prediction to ensure feasible solutions are ground-truth feasible.

arxiv-2509-24791.title: Vision Function Layer in Multimodal LLMs
arxiv-2509-24791.creator: Cheng Shi, Yizhou Yu, Sibei Yang
arxiv-2509-24791.description: Abstract This study identifies that visual-related functional decoding is distributed across different decoder layers in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Typically, each function, such as counting, grounding, or OCR recognition, narrows down to two or three layers, which we define as Vision Function Layers (VFL).

arxiv-2602-00425.title: Segment-Level Attribution for Selective Learning of Long Reasoning Traces
arxiv-2602-00425.creator: Siyuan Wang, Yanchen Liu, Xiang Ren

pmc-10606436.title: Non-Hermitian Floquet Topological Matter—A Review
pmc-10606436.creator: Longwen Zhou, Da-Jian Zhang, Adam Gadomski
pmc-10606436.description: The past few years have witnessed a surge of interest in non-Hermitian Floquet topological matter due to its exotic properties resulting from the interplay between driving fields and non-Hermiticity. The present review sums up our studies on non-Hermitian Floquet topological matter in one and two spatial dimensions.

pmc-10768552.title: Prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus and associated factors among women receiving antenatal care at a tertiary hospital in South-Western Uganda
pmc-10768552.creator: Irene Kahimakazi, Yarine Fajardo Tornes, Leevan Tibaijuka, Hamson Kanyesigye, Joshua Kiptoo, Musa Kayondo, Joseph Ngonzi, Kwame Adu-Bonsaffoh, Lenard Abesiga, Henry Mark Lugobe
pmc-10768552.description: Introduction: gestational diabetes mellitus is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality among pregnant women worldwide. We aimed to determine the prevalence and factors associated with gestational diabetes mellitus among women attending the antenatal care clinic at a tertiary care hospital in South-Western Uganda.

pmc-11437398.title: Structural Heterogeneity of the Rabies Virus Virion
pmc-11437398.creator: Xiaoying Cai, Kang Zhou, Ana Lucia Alvarez-Cabrera, Zhu Si, Hui Wang, Yao He, Cally Li, Z. Hong Zhou
pmc-11437398.description: Rabies virus (RABV) is among the first recognized viruses of public health concern and has historically contributed to the development of viral vaccines. Despite these significances, the three-dimensional structure of the RABV virion remains unknown due to the challenges in isolating structurally homogenous virion samples in sufficient quantities needed for structural investigation.

pmc-11457477.title: Migratory autolysosome disposal mitigates lysosome damage
pmc-11457477.creator: Takami Sho, Ying Li, Haifeng Jiao, Li Yu
pmc-11457477.description: This study unveils migratory autolysosome disposal, a response to lysosomal damage where cells expel LAMP1-LC3 positive structures via autolysosome exocytosis, requiring autophagy machinery, SNARE proteins, and cell migration. This novel mechanism highlights the intricate relationship between cell migration, organelle quality control, and extracellular vesicle release.

pmc-11634854.title: The effector function of mucosal associated invariant T cells alters with aging and is regulated by RORγt
pmc-11634854.creator: Zhi Yang, Banxin Luo, Minhuan Li, Ziyun He, Chuanfu Ren, Xin Chen, Xing Kang, Hong Chen, En Xu, Wenxian Guan, Xuefeng Xia
pmc-11634854.description: IntroductionMucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are a predominant subset of innate-like T cells in humans, characterized by diverse gene expression profiles and functional capabilities. However, the factors influencing the transcriptomes and effector functions of MAIT cells, particularly at mucosal barriers, remain largely unclear.

pmc-12640326.title: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome is the most frequent cardiovascular autonomic disorder following COVID-19 infection or vaccination
pmc-12640326.creator: Fabian Leys, Mara Verginer, Elias Kirchler, Loraine Marino, Georg Goebel, Nicole Campese, Sabine Eschlböck, Susanne Duerr, Gregor Broessner, Atbin Djamshidian-Tehrani, Anna Heidbreder, Birgit Högl, Maria-Sophie Rothmund-Grenier, Katharina Hüfner, Sarah Iglseder, Wolfgang Löscher, Ambra Stefani, Juli
pmc-12640326.description: BackgroundCardiovascular autonomic disorders (CAD) were described following COVID-19 infection and vaccination, but previous reports were limited in size and follow-up. Here, we aimed to investigate the type and frequency of newly diagnosed and exacerbated CAD following COVID-19 infection or vaccination, and assessed their associated autonomic and non-autonomic complaints, applied treatment, and clinical outcome at last follow-up.

pmc-12641794.title: Breast Cancer Progression and Its Theranostic Management via Folate-Directed Targeting of Glycoprotein Receptor
pmc-12641794.creator: Koyeli Girigoswami, Agnishwar Girigoswami, Jean-Marie Exbrayat, Ravi P Sahu
pmc-12641794.description: Breast cancer continues to rank among the most common and complex cancers worldwide. A promising approach is the direct delivery of drugs to cancer cells via specially designed nanocarriers that can target specific receptors on their surface, like folate receptors.

pmc-12656413.title: Beta-Blockers as Potential Adjuvants in Melanoma Treatment
pmc-12656413.creator: Laura Rama, Mónica Almeida, Jiya Jose, Maria de Lourdes Pereira, Miguel Oliveira
pmc-12656413.description: Melanoma, in advanced stages, is the most invasive type of skin cancer, with currently available treatments showing limited efficiency. The number of melanoma cancer cases is expected to increase in the coming years, emphasizing the need for more efficient therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12987331.title: Multi-Omics Reveals Domestication-Associated Shifts in Phosphorus Adaptation Strategies in Tomato
pmc-12987331.creator: Shuai Yuan, Yujie Yang, Yiyong Zhu, Xianqing Jia, Jiahong Yu
pmc-12987331.description: Phosphorus (P) limitation is a major selective pressure in plant evolution and a persistent constraint on modern crop production. However, how domestication has reshaped P adaptation strategies remains poorly understood. Here, we compared wild (Solanum pimpinellifolium) and cultivated (Solanum lycopersicum) tomatoes under contrasting P conditions using integrated physiological, ionomic, and transcriptomic analyses.

pmc-13095305.title: Predictive factors for the development of urethral stricture in patients undergoing holmium laser enucleation of the prostate: A retrospective study
pmc-13095305.creator: Ferec Efendioğlu, Cihat Özcan, Zafer Tokatli
pmc-13095305.description: This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of urethral stricture after holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) and to assess the safety of the procedure. We retrospectively reviewed data from 202 patients who underwent HoLEP. Patients were divided into 2 groups: those with urethral stricture (group 2) and those without (group 1).

pmc-13147006.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A966 EXPLORING PATIENTS’ EXPERIENCES OF SECONDARY PREVENTION AFTER STROKE: A SURVEY STUDY
pmc-13147006.creator: Sarah-Jane Byrne, David Williams, Declan Patton, Frances Horgan
pmc-13147006.description: Background and aimsStroke secondary prevention focuses on reducing the likelihood of future strokes by addressing underlying risk factors and lifestyle factors that contribute to stroke. Nurses play an important role in stroke secondary prevention and recently as key team members in early supported discharge (ESD) teams.

pmc-13543583.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and systemic immune-inflammation index are associated with left ventricular hypertrophy in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients
pmc-13543583.creator: Peipei Xu, Kangwen Lu, Jingjing Liu, Xiaoqin Zhao, Renyue Hu, Yi Sun, Jie Yuan, Yunjuan Gu, Chen Qian, Xinlei Wang

pmc-13574541.title: Spatiotemporal immune heterogeneity and precision immunotherapy for ovarian cancer
pmc-13574541.creator: Xinfeng Yang, Yida Wang, Haiyue You, Jingyi Gao, Yangkun Feng, Feng Zhang, Yan Zhang, Bing Zhang, Shaojie Zhao, Yanfang Gu
pmc-13574541.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: The clinical benefit of immunotherapy in ovarian cancer (OC) remains limited. The primary reason is not simply a lack of immune activation, but rather the marked spatiotemporal heterogeneity of the tumour immune microenvironment.

pmc-13601742.title: Comparing the Impact of Tetrahydrocannabinol on 30‐Day Readmission Rates and Hospital Length of Stay in Patients With Depression
pmc-13601742.creator: Mohammed E. Khedr, Yunjin Lee, Muhammed A. Mirza, Humberto Jimenez, Daniel Greer
pmc-13601742.description: Background and ObjectivesDelta‐9‐tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive constituent of cannabis, continues to be critically evaluated for its potential therapeutic efficacy and associated safety concerns in major depressive disorder (MDD). Length of stay and readmission rates are key indicators of treatment response and prognosis. With rising cannabis use, understanding the effects of THC is essential.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Establishment There is hereby established an Environmental Education and Training Program.
